subject: Intermittent tenant queue drain — entitlement & postmortem request (FlutterChain)
messages:
From: Alex Turner <alex.turner@flutterchain.com>
To: Sean Gallagher <sean.gallagher@redwood.ai>
Cc: ops@flutterchain.com
Date: Sun, 1 Nov 2026 01:12:00 -0700
Subject: Sudden request failures during nightly batch — possible queue drain

Hi Sean,

We observed a cluster of 500/502 errors during our scheduled midnight batch window (00:55–01:20 PST) this morning. The failures look like downstream queue drains — the requests hit the service and then are dropped rather than queued. This affected approximately 12k of our requests (roughly 1.7% of traffic during the window).

We've attached a small sample of failed request ids and a trace from our side. Can you confirm whether this qualifies as an availability SLO violation for a single-tenant degradation? If so, what evidence do you need from us to open an entitlement claim and start a postmortem?

We rely on Redwood Dedicated for predictable throughput; this window had material business impact to our batch reconciliations.

Thanks,
Alex Turner
Head of Platform, FlutterChain
attachments: flutterchain_queue_drain_trace.jsonl, sample_requests_20261101.csv

From: Sean Gallagher <sean.gallagher@redwood.ai>
To: Alex Turner <alex.turner@flutterchain.com>
Cc: laura_bennett@redwood.ai, marissa_cole@redwood.ai
Date: Sun, 1 Nov 2026 02:02:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Sudden request failures during nightly batch — possible queue drain

Hi Alex — thanks for the quick heads-up and for including the traces. Sorry for the disruption.

Short answers up-front:
- We will treat this as an SLA claim path and open an entitlement review.
- We need both the sample request ids (you included) and a compact telemetry bundle from your tenant showing request timestamps, status codes, and client IDs for the 00:45–01:30 window. That helps correlate tenant-side drops with our backend ingress/queue metrics.
- Please confirm whether you were on Dedicated pool "dedicated-us-west-2-4" for that workload.

Operational next steps from our side: I’ve looped in Laura (SRE lead) and Marissa (Customer Success) to assemble an evidence packet and evaluate proportional credit if the incident meets SLO breach criteria. We’ll also prepare a postmortem invite once we validate the timeline.

Can you send the telemetry bundle and a short note on whether you made any config changes or deployments in the prior hour? I’ll create an internal ticket and share the log pull instructions.

—Sean
Sean Gallagher
Head of Reliability, Redwood Inference
Redwood Inference | sean.gallagher@redwood.ai

From: Alex Turner <alex.turner@flutterchain.com>
To: Sean Gallagher <sean.gallagher@redwood.ai>
Cc: ops@flutterchain.com
Date: Sun, 1 Nov 2026 03:10:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Sudden request failures during nightly batch — possible queue drain

Sean,

Thanks — attaching the full compact bundle now (shared to your Drive link) and confirming the tenant was pinned to dedicated-us-west-2-4. No deployments or config changes from our side between 23:30–01:30. We did see a transient spike in batch concurrency (~20% above normal) but nothing unprecedented.

Drive link: https://drive.flutterchain.com/telemetry/queue-dump-20261101 (shared with redwood-sre@redwood.ai)

Let us know if you need additional logs. We’d like to get an estimate on how long the entitlement review will take — we need to plan customer-facing comms.

Alex

From: Laura Bennett <laura_bennett@redwood.ai>
To: Sean Gallagher <sean.gallagher@redwood.ai>, Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>
Date: Sun, 1 Nov 2026 09:30:00 -07:00
Subject: FW: Sudden request failures during nightly batch — possible queue drain

Team — quick triage notes after an initial look at the bundle Alex shared:

- Correlation: ingress metrics show a sharp drain in the tenant's request queue on node rwd-gpu-12 at 00:58:12 PST; aggregated queue depth dropped to near-zero for ~9 minutes while backend CPU utilization remained normal. Downstream RPCs returned 500 when requests retried and were routed off-cone.
- Likely cause: a transient connector thread stuck on a partial epoll wake path leading to dropped entries in the per-tenant queue; reproduces in lab when forcing high concurrency + small prefetched KV windows.
- SLO evaluation: Impact window = 00:58:12–01:07:25 PST; error rate for tenant during that window exceeds the 99.9% availability target (we compute ~1.8% failed token generation). Based on contract, this looks like an eligible event for proportional credit for Dedicated customers.

Attachments: short evidence extract and timing map (attached as postmortem-draft-template.md). I recommend we:
1) Confirm eligibility with finance for proportional credit calculation (Marissa),
2) Schedule a postmortem with FlutterChain and SRE/pass around raw logs,
3) Prepare a remediation plan to push the connector thread fix and a warmup guard for high concurrency.

Marissa — can you lead the customer comms and confirm what remedy band we should propose (pro-rata credit vs one-time service credit)?

Laura
Laura Bennett
Senior SRE, Redwood Inference

From: Sean Gallagher <sean.gallagher@redwood.ai>
To: Alex Turner <alex.turner@flutterchain.com>
Cc: laura_bennett@redwood.ai, marissa_cole@redwood.ai
Date: Mon, 2 Nov 2026 10:00:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Sudden request failures during nightly batch — possible queue drain

Alex — following our internal review, we’ve opened an entitlement ticket and preliminarily confirmed the incident window as 2026-11-01T00:58:12–2026-11-01T01:07:25 PST.

What we will deliver in the next 72 hours:
- Evidence packet (correlated ingress + tenant telemetry), included as a Drive bundle: https://drive.redwood.com/FlutterChain/telemetry/queue-dump-20261101
- Draft postmortem and proposed remediation (we attached a template and a brief timing map).
- A credit recommendation to Finance (Marissa will follow up on the exact pro-rata calculation).

Proposed meeting: Postmortem triage on Tue Nov 3, 2026 at 09:00 PST — 30 minutes. Please confirm availability; we’ll send a calendar invite and a read-ahead (postmortem-draft-template.md).

Thanks again for the fast collaboration — we’ll aim to be transparent with logs and the remediation timeline.

—Sean
Sean Gallagher
Head of Reliability, Redwood Inference
attachments: postmortem-draft-template.md
